title: receipts project config
description: Project-specific plumbing for the receipts gates. Produced by `receipts init` (detect -> confirm -> write); rarely hand-authored. The gate LOGIC ships generic; this file only tells receipts how to build/test/reach THIS project and what marks a fix-claim.

claim.description: How a PR claims to fix an issue, and how it honestly downgrades.

issue_link.description: Regex matching how a PR links the issue it fixes.

require_receipt_for.description: When the enforcer requires a receipt. 'issue-link' (default): only a fix-claim (a PR matching issue_link) must carry one - a PR with no issue link and no work-type passes untouched. 'any-source-change' (strict): a PR that changes production source (excluding docs / tests / CI / config) must ALSO carry a receipt, an honest downgrade tag, or an explicit work-type - closing the 'omit the issue link => silent green' bypass.

downgrade_tags.description: Tags that mark a PR as NOT claiming a clean fix (the honesty ladder); these pass the gate but are tracked, not treated as 'fixed'.

require_receipt_lock.description: The untrusted-agent posture: every verified claim must carry a `receipt-lock: <sha256>` line matching the receipt content at head. The acceptance test is authored/approved by a trusted party FIRST (`receipts lock` prints the line), and the agent's only job is to make the LOCKED rubric pass - it cannot weaken, replace, or 'adjust' it. Without the lock, whoever writes the code also grades it.

build.description: How receipts binds to the build under test and (optionally) the deployed app.

sha_source.description: How to confirm which commit the build/deploy carries (G3). 'none' = no deploy; verify against the built artifact + test run. STATUS: read today by the agent-side Stop hook ('none' / 'ci-artifact' stands the deployed-build backstop down for a repo with no URL deploy); the CI enforcer does not query the deployments API yet (design in enforcer/GENERALIZATION.md).

platform.description: Detected deploy platform (informational), e.g. vercel | railway | netlify | fly | render | none.

deploy_host_patterns.description: Host globs that count as 'pointed at the deployed build' (for optional live-drive).

verify_against.description: Which environment the enforcer re-verifies on (a key of `environments`).

verify.description: How to run the receipt: the carried red->green acceptance test. The PRIMARY verification; uses the project's own test framework + CI auth. Required for the ENFORCER (it errors without test_command); an agent-home config (skills + session cwd, no code repo) may omit this whole block - that is why `verify` is not a top-level required field.

test_command.description: Run the carried acceptance test(s). Placeholders, because runners SELECT differently: `{test}` = the changed test FILE path(s), quoted (jest / pytest / rspec / mix take paths); `{test_dirs}` = the unique './dir's of those files (`go test` selects by package, not file); `{test_classes}` = the basenames sans extension, comma-joined (Maven surefire's -Dtest=). A file path fed to a name-selector (-run / -Dtest= / --filter) matches nothing and exits 0 - a red phase that ran no test.

suite_command.description: Run the full suite (G9 full-scope green: the enforcer runs this on head after the narrow receipt, so a regression in code the changed test never exercises is caught, not just the changed test).

require_fresh_base.description: G8 fresh base: whether the enforcer flags a branch that is behind its base (a green earned on a stale base is green on code that won't ship). 'warn' (default) surfaces it without failing the check; 'block' fails it; 'off' disables.

on_load_error_red.description: What to do when the receipt's RED on base is a load/collection error (import / syntax / no-tests), not an assertion failure - a red that may not prove the symptom (the test may just import code that only exists on head). 'warn' (default): surface it, still allow. 'block': fail it, EXCEPT when the PR is `work-type: feature` (a feature's test is legitimately red until the feature exists).

command_timeout_ms.description: Per-command timeout (milliseconds) for the test/suite commands the enforcer runs. A hung test is killed and reported (timed_out in the receipt) rather than holding the CI job to its own ceiling. DEFAULT: 20 minutes (1200000). An explicit 0 disables (the job's timeout still applies).

receipt_runs.description: Run the receipt N times on each side: the red must be red N/N on base and the green green N/N on head. A FLAKY receipt can manufacture a fake red (a green test that flaked red on base) or pass a broken fix (a red that flaked green on head) - N > 1 rejects nondeterministic receipts as unproven (G0/G9). Default 1 (single run, prior behavior).

live_drive.description: OPTIONAL advanced: a command/script that drives the deployed app for symptoms a unit/e2e test can't cover. null = not used (the carried test is enough). RESERVED: declared for the roadmap; the enforcer does not execute it yet.

browser_receipt.description: OPTIONAL web-medium adapter: run a browser/e2e script (Playwright, Cypress, etc.) against the PR's PREVIEW DEPLOYMENT as a HEAD-ONLY acceptance check. IMPORTANT - this is NOT a red->green receipt: a preview deploys only the HEAD build, so there is no base preview to run it red against. It is a G1/G3/G5-shaped acceptance check (does the fixed behavior actually work on the live deploy) that runs IN ADDITION to the carried red->green receipt and NEVER substitutes for it. Playwright is NOT a dependency of receipts: the consuming repo brings its own e2e stack; receipts only resolves the preview URL, exports it as RECEIPTS_PREVIEW_URL, runs `command`, and folds the exit code into the verdict. Runs isolated after the main dance - a thrown error / unreachable preview degrades to a WARN, never a crash and (unless mode:block) never a hard fail.

command.description: How to run the browser/e2e script against the preview. It reads the preview URL from the RECEIPTS_PREVIEW_URL env var receipts exports (e.g. a playwright.config baseURL, or `page.goto(process.env.RECEIPTS_PREVIEW_URL)`). Must be a single command whose own exit is the result (exit-masking `;`/`||`/pipe/`&` is rejected - a green from a masked exit cannot be trusted, G9); wrap complex flows in a script.

url_source.description: How to resolve the preview URL. 'env' (default): read it from an env var (url_env). 'github-deployment': query the GitHub deployments API for the PR head sha's environment_url (uses GITHUB_TOKEN + GITHUB_REPOSITORY, both provided inside the Action; works for Vercel and other platforms that post deployments). 'command': run url_cmd and read the first http(s) URL it prints. Every path degrades HONESTLY when the URL can't be resolved - a distinct 'could not resolve preview URL' WARN, never a silent pass.

url_env.description: For url_source: 'env' - the env var to READ the preview URL from (your deploy step or a prior job sets it). Independent of the FIXED RECEIPTS_PREVIEW_URL name that receipts EXPORTS to `command` (so the script itself is url_source-agnostic). Default: RECEIPTS_PREVIEW_URL (set it yourself if you use the env source).

url_cmd.description: For url_source: 'command' - a command that PRINTS the preview URL (the first http(s) line of its stdout is used). E.g. a Vercel/Netlify CLI call, or a `gh` query. Exit-masking is rejected (G9). Used only when url_source is 'command'.

mode.description: 'warn' (default): a failing browser receipt (or a preview-is-not-the-head-build sha mismatch) surfaces as a WARN without failing the check - the preview being flaky/unreachable is often infra, not the PR's fault, and the red->green receipt is the primary gate. 'block': a definitive failure (the command ran and exited non-zero against a resolved preview) fails the check. Honest-degradation cases (URL unresolved, adapter error) are ALWAYS a WARN regardless of mode - you cannot block on a check that could not run.

timeout_ms.description: Per-command timeout (milliseconds) for the browser command and the url_cmd. Defaults to verify.command_timeout_ms (20 min). A hung browser run is killed and reported (timed_out), not held to the job ceiling.

degrade.description: Honest behavior when the symptom cannot be re-verified. Never silent-pass; never block-all.

on_no_receipt.description: What to do when a fix-claim carries no re-runnable acceptance test.

on_unreachable_build.description: What to do when the deployed build can't be reached for re-verification. RESERVED: declared for the live-drive design in enforcer/GENERALIZATION.md; not read by the enforcer yet.

gates.description: Which gates apply to this project, and per-gate selectors. Gates are referenced by ID (G0-G13) - the shared vocabulary across the spec, the `gates` skill, the Stop hooks, and the enforcer. `receipts init` writes a safe default (all on); disable the gates that do not fit (e.g. G10 in a single repo with no split deploy, or the deploy-surface gates in a library with no deploy). The skill reads this to know which gates to apply; the enforcer reads it to know which checks to run.

medium.description: The software type, so the gates apply in the right terms - a 'surface' / 'value' / 'terminal action' means something different for a web app vs an API vs a library vs a CLI vs a data pipeline vs infra. A hint the agent reads alongside references/MEDIA.md; free-form and expandable. Common values: web, api, service, library, cli, mobile, desktop, data, ml, infra, database, smart-contract, browser-extension, embedded, game, unknown.

work_type.description: OPTIONAL default work type (fix / feature / migration / refactor / chore). Usually LEFT UNSET - work type is per-PR, not per-project (most repos mix), so the agent determines it per task and a PR signals it with a `work-type:` line in its body. It sets what the receipt asserts (the acceptance criterion), and for refactor/chore it inverts the receipt to 'the full suite stays green' (no behavior change). See references/WORK-TYPES.md.

enabled.description: Which gates run here: "all", or an explicit array of gate IDs (G0-G13).

disabled.description: Gate IDs to turn off even if `enabled` includes them; takes precedence over `enabled`.

G6.description: Surface coverage - the 'sweep the twins' assist. Catches a pattern applied to SOME sibling surfaces but not all (an 'app-wide' change that is actually partial). Two mechanisms: declared `surfaces` (a glob + a required marker substring, any language) and a built-in JS/TS heuristic - any AFFORDANCE (a component, hook, attribute, prop, call, or import - any identifier that is not a ubiquitous plumbing word) rolled out to >=2 same-named siblings flags the twins that missed it. Runs on every PR with a diff.

mode.description: What an incomplete rollout does: warn (default) or block.

auto.description: Enable the JS/TS import-rollout heuristic (no config needed). Set false to rely only on declared `surfaces`.

surfaces.description: Declared surface families: each is a set of files (glob) that must all carry a marker (substring). Encodes an 'app-wide' invariant the enforcer re-checks - language-agnostic.

glob.description: Files in the family, e.g. 'src/**/*Table.tsx'. Supports * and **.

marker.description: Substring every family member must contain, e.g. 'Pagination' or 'usePagination' or 'LIMIT'.

always.description: Check coverage on every PR (a standing invariant), not only when a PR touches the marker. Default false.

G7.description: Dependent-test-selection. The enforcer computes the NEW dependents of the changed source (a freshly-added consumer file, or a freshly-added import edge) and re-runs their co-located tests on head, catching an integration regression the carried receipt never exercises. Built-in support: a JS/TS import scan; for any stack, point `graph` at a consumer graph.

mode.description: What a failing NEW-dependent test does: warn (default - the reverse-dependency set is heuristic) or block.

graph.description: Optional path (in the repo, read at head) to a consumer graph JSON: an object mapping each importer file to the list of files it imports. Used to compute dependents for stacks the built-in JS/TS scanner does not cover.

verify_all_dependents.description: Widen the scope from NEW dependents (the default - the freshly-routed consumer) to EVERY consumer of the changed surface. Use for high-blast-radius changes; slower and noisier.

integration_branch.description: The branch whose tip 'fresh base' is measured against (e.g. main, dev-django). The enforcer also reads the PR's base automatically; this documents the intended integration branch for the agent.

G10.description: Rollout-compatibility selectors. The enforcer back-compat-checks changed contract artifacts on a PR (built-in: OpenAPI/Swagger/AsyncAPI/JSON-Schema get a structural breaking-diff; GraphQL/proto/yaml get a 'changed - verify manually' warning).

contract_paths.description: Extra globs of contract artifacts to back-compat-check, on top of the built-in detection (e.g. "api/schema.json", "**/*.proto", "proto/**").

mode.description: What a detected breaking contract change does: warn (default) or block.

contract_pairs.description: Producer/consumer halves whose contract must stay compatible across the deploy window.

G11.description: Referee integrity - the 'don't shoot the referee' gate. Flags a PR that DELETES test files, adds skip/focus markers (.skip / xit / @pytest.mark.skip / t.Skip / @Disabled / .only), or rewrites snapshot artifacts: a green earned by shrinking the suite's assertion power proves nothing. An honest `test-removal: <why>` line in the PR body acknowledges intentional removals (tracked, never blocked). Runs statically on every PR.

mode.description: What an unacknowledged test deletion / added skip does: warn (default) or block. Snapshot churn always warns only.

G12.description: Fix the cause, not the alarm - the silencing assist. On a fix-claim, flags a diff that REMOVES throw/raise statements or ADDS empty/swallowing catches: the symptom may be gone because its DETECTOR is (a permission check deleted to cure a 403, an exception swallowed to cure an error toast). Heuristic - some fixes legitimately remove an over-strict check - so it asks; the judgment is agent-side (the skill).

mode.description: What a silencing-shaped diff does: warn (default - the heuristic asks a question) or block.

G13.description: Claim-scope congruence - the receipt must EXERCISE the diff. The red->green proves the receipt relates to the change; it says nothing about the other changed lines riding along. With a coverage command configured, the enforcer runs it on head, parses lcov, and lists changed production lines never executed by any test. OPT-IN (coverage tooling is stack-specific and slower); no coverage_command = the gate does not run.

coverage_command.description: Command that runs the suite with coverage and writes an lcov file (e.g. `npx c8 --reporter=lcov npm test`, `coverage run -m pytest && coverage lcov`).

lcov_path.description: Where the lcov file lands, relative to the repo root (default: coverage/lcov.info).

mode.description: What uncovered changed lines do: warn (default) or block.

G14.description: Receipt strength - the mutation referee. Red->green proves the receipt notices THE fix, not that it would notice a WRONG one (a receipt asserting 'not the old value' goes green for any change). G14 deliberately breaks each changed line (a small operator set: flipped comparisons, &&/||, true/false, numbers nudged) and requires the receipt to go red; a SURVIVOR is a changed line the receipt cannot tell from broken. Runs whenever a receipt exists; capped and diff-scoped, so it costs a handful of receipt re-runs.

mode.description: What a surviving mutant does: warn (default - a survivor can be an equivalent mutant) or block (the untrusted-agent posture).

max_mutants.description: Budget: at most this many mutants are tried, round-robin across changed files (breadth before depth). Each costs one receipt re-run.

G17.description: The honesty ladder's feedback loop. A downgrade is honest per item and blind in aggregate: N individually-defensible downgrades sharing ONE reason are not N unlucky items, they are one capability the process never built. Tally downgrades by (reason x surface-class) across the run and, past the threshold, name the missing capability in the run summary. Surfacing only - it must never block an item, because blocking converts an honest downgrade into pressure to claim 'fixed' instead.

downgrade_threshold.description: How many times one downgrade reason may recur within a run, keyed by (reason x surface-class), before the run summary must name the missing capability.

agent.description: How the agent-side Stop hooks bind to THIS project: which skills are fix/build loops (watched by the trajectory reminder + carrying the kb touchpoints), what extra by-value-query patterns count, and which tracker statuses mean 'fixed'. The hooks ship generic defaults; these MERGE OVER them (never replace the generics, so a clean install still works). Written by `receipts init`. Deploy-host patterns live in `build.deploy_host_patterns` (shared with the enforcer).

loop_skills.description: Skill names that are fix/build loops: the trajectory-reminder watches these (append-on-exit) and they carry the kb query/append touchpoints. The shipped 'gates' plus any project loop skills.

staging_query_patterns.description: Extra substrings / MCP-tool names that count as a by-value query against the deployed build (e.g. a DB proxy host, a query tool), on top of the generic defaults.

closeout_fixed_statuses.description: Tracker status strings that mean 'claimed fixed' (e.g. 'Fixed - Pending Retest', 'Verified', 'Closed'); the verification gate treats a status update to one of these as a fix close-out.

repo_name.description: Default repo tag for trajectory-kb appends (the agent may override per append).

evidence.description: What kind of deployed-build evidence the Stop hook's verification gate accepts at a fix close-out. 'heuristic' (default, key absent): the pattern-matched signals count - a navigate to a deploy host + a screenshot / DOM read / by-value query. 'live-receipt' (opt-in strict): ONLY a valid `receipts/live-receipt@1` (produced by `receipts observe`) with met:true AND a build binding (artifact.kind != 'none') satisfies the gate - a machine-validated probe of the live build, not 'a screenshot happened'. The block message then tells the agent the exact `receipts observe ...` command to run. See spec/LIVE-RECEIPT.md.

trajectory_store.description: Where the trajectory memory lives - this decides WHO it serves. 'home' (default): ~/.claude/mcp-servers/trajectory-kb/data/trajectories.jsonl - private, per-machine, aggregates across your repos. 'repo': <repo>/.receipts/trajectories.jsonl - COMMIT it and the whole team inherits every recorded trap and dead end (append-only JSONL merges trivially). Any other value: an explicit path, resolved against this config's directory.

memory_inject.description: Whether the SessionStart hook (session-memory.mjs) PUSHES prior trajectory scars into a new session's context WITHOUT the agent having to query the kb - so a weak agent that never asks still arrives warned. 'on' (default when a receipts.config.json is present): at session start it reads the trajectory store, picks up to ~5 most-relevant entries for THIS repo (failures first, one per surface_key), and injects a compact (~1500-char-capped) summary as additionalContext. 'off': disables the injection. A repo with NO receipts config at all gets zero injection regardless (never opted in). Read only by the agent-side hook, not the CI enforcer.

tripwires.description: In-session PreToolUse guards (the `pre-gates.mjs` hook) that fire AT the risky action, between the Stop-hook backstop and the CI enforcer. Each raises the weak-agent floor without waiting for a stop-cycle or a PR. All default to 'deny' with an EXPLICIT, greppable escape (an honesty tag in the command / edit - `RECEIPTS_ACK=<why>`, `RECEIPTS_TRIPWIRE=off`, `--no-verify-receipts`, or a `test-removal: <why>` note), never a silent skip. Ship generic; this only tunes THIS project.

commit_unverified.description: The commit-without-verification tripwire (Bash `git commit`): a commit that lands right after a production-source edit with NO test / receipt command run in between is denied - a commit is a claim it works (G0/G9). 'deny' (default): block with the escape instructions. 'off': disable. 'warn' is accepted but is a NO-OP at PreToolUse (there is no reliable agent-visible warn channel there) - use 'deny' to enforce or 'off' to disable.

g11_live.description: The G11-live referee tripwire (Edit/Write/MultiEdit on a TEST file): editing a test that was seen FAILING earlier this session with no passing run since is the 'shoot the referee' move - fix the code, not the test (G11). 'deny' (default): block unless the edit carries a `test-removal: <why>` note or a `RECEIPTS_ACK`. 'off': disable. 'warn' is a NO-OP (see commit_unverified).

test_command_patterns.description: Extra regex patterns (matched against the Bash command string) that count as 'ran the code / produced a receipt' for the commit tripwire, on top of the generic defaults (npm/pnpm/yarn test, node --test, vitest/jest/mocha/playwright, pytest/tox/nox, go/cargo/mvn/gradle test, rspec, mix test, phpunit, dotnet test, receipts observe/verify, ...). Add a bespoke runner here, e.g. "run-checks\\.sh".
